# Character voice bible

## Register system
Two address forms in Hungarian: **tegezés** (informal "you" — te/téged, -sz/-l/-d verb endings) and **magázás** (formal "you" — Ön/Önt, -ik-type polite verb endings, or the slightly less stiff Maga/Maguk). Not interchangeable mid-conversation with the same addressee unless the source itself deliberately signals a register shift — if a character's relationship to the player changes, that should already be visible in how the source is written, not invented by the translator.

**Default by content type** (full rule in lang-style.md — this table is the per-character reference):
- UI / tutorial / system messages → magázás. No character voice applies here at all.
- Dialogue → tegezés, unless the specific character below is marked otherwise.

Per-character overrides below. A speaker not listed here defaults to tegezés with no other specified traits — add a row once they have enough lines that a consistent voice actually matters.

| Character | Register | Traits | Avoid |
|---|---|---|---|
| Kael | tegezés — informal, blunt, short sentences | Drops articles/pronouns where Hungarian allows it without sounding broken ("Megyek." not "Én megyek."); reacts before explaining; short clauses, rarely more than one subordinate clause deep | Flowery/literary phrasing; magázás under any circumstance — even addressing a superior, Kael stays informal, that's a character trait, not an oversight |
| Narrator | No direct addressee in most lines — descriptive/expository, not a conversation partner. Tegezés if a line does directly address the player (rare). | Complete sentences, factual register, past tense for recounted events; avoids first person entirely | Slang, humor, breaking the fourth wall unless the source line explicitly does |

## Adding a new character
When a new named speaker appears often enough to need a row: default to tegezés unless the source context clearly establishes otherwise (nobility, a strict authority figure, an antagonist deliberately keeping distance, or a formal system/AI voiced as a person are the usual reasons for magázás instead). Write the register out explicitly even when it's the default ("tegezés," not left blank) — so a reviewer can tell "unset" from "deliberately default" at a glance.
